title: Runtime scaling experiment protocol and benchmark checklist
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
SUMMARY
This page defines a repeatable experiment protocol and checklist for scaling experiments on the Redwood inference runtime. It combines workload construction, kernel scheduling knobs, telemetry targets, profiling hooks, acceptance criteria and rollback/runbook steps so teams can: (1) validate autoscaling/autotune changes, (2) quantify cost/latency trade-offs from scheduler/kernel changes, and (3) produce reproducible reports for release decisions.

GOALS
- Provide a canonical experiment recipe for both synthetic and production-replay workloads.
- Make outcomes comparable across hardware generations and model families.
- Capture actionable metrics: P50/P95/P99 latencies, tail token latency, per-kernel time breakdown, GPU SM utilization, memory pressure, and throughput vs. cost.

SCOPE AND NON-SCOPE
- Scope: inference-serving control plane + serving runtime up to kernel level (no downstream app logic). Includes KV cache behavior, batching, and preemption interactions.
- Non-scope: training workloads, network fabric microbenchmarks outside the host (separate infra tests).

OWNERSHIP AND ROLES
- Experiment owner (run): eng-serving-runtime bench lead (default: Aisha Kapoor).
- Scheduler/kernel SME: Marcus Li.
- SRE/observability: Daniel Rios.
- Reviewer for final report: product performance PM.

PREREQUISITES
1) Baseline images and hashes: store the exact runtime container tag and kernel artifacts used. Example: runtime:v2026-11-03-hash-abc123.
2) Calibration harness: benchctl v2.1+ installed on a bastion in the same region as the GPU fleet.
3) Telemetry: perf-trace and kernel-timings collectors running at sampling=100ms for baseline; hwm profiling for deep dives.

MEASUREMENTS (METRICS TO CAPTURE)
- Client-side: request rate (RPS), tokens/sec, request size distribution, sequence length histogram.
- Latency: request P50/P95/P99, token tail latency (99.9th token).
- Runtime: kernel time breakdown (attention, matmul, softmax, kv-lookup), scheduling queue wait, batching latency.
- System: GPU SM% (utilization), GPU memory used/fragmentation, host CPU steal, NVLink/PCIe stalls.
- Cost proxies: GPU-minutes, estimated token cost (from autotune model).

EXPERIMENT DESIGN
1) Workload shapes (run each shape for 10 minutes stable window):
   a) Uniform short: sequence=64, batch policy=auto, prefix cache disabled.
   b) Long-tail: 70% seq=32, 20% seq=512, 10% seq=1024.
   c) Realistic replay: traffic replay of 1 hour of production sample anonymized (use replay-id).
   d) Burst + steady: 30s burst at 3x normal RPS followed by steady 5m at nominal RPS.
2) Batching matrix: explicit batch sizes [1,4,8,16] and dynamic batching on/off.
3) KV cache modes: cold start (cache miss), warm (80% hit), degraded (50% hit).
4) Priority mix: 90% normal, 10% high-priority; enable preemption to observe graceful migration.

STEP-BY-STEP RUNBOOK (canonical sequence)
1) Snapshot baseline: capture system snapshot and store under s3://redwood-benchshots/{run-id}/baseline.json.
2) Deploy experiment image to a dedicated test pool. Use canary routing to avoid customer traffic.
3) Start perf-trace collectors: "perfctl start --target=pool-a --sampling-ms=100 --out={run-id}".
4) Warmup: run 2 warmup cycles per shape (5 minutes each) to populate KV cache and JIT kernels.
5) Execute shapes and batching matrix in deterministic order.
6) After each shape run, capture kernel timeline: "kern-dump --run {run-id} --out {run-id}/kernels.trace".
7) Post-run: run profiler aggregation job and produce a PDF report using bench-report v1.3.

EXAMPLE BENCHMARK CONFIG (YAML)
```
name: scaling-experiment-2026-02-01
pool: test-gpu-pool-a
model: llama-7b-quant-v2
shapes:
  - name: uniform-short
    seq: 64
    duration: 600
  - name: long-tail
    mix: [0.7,0.2,0.1]
    seqs: [32,512,1024]
batching:
  static_sizes: [1,4,8,16]
  dynamic: true
kv_cache_modes: [cold,warm,degraded]
priority_mix: {normal:0.9,high:0.1}
```

QUANTITATIVE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- No P99 regression > 15% relative to baseline for production-replay shape.
- Token tail latency (99.9th token) must not increase by > 20ms when enabling dynamic batching.
- Kernel preemption should not cause more than 2% increase in error rate or timed-out requests.
- GPU SM utilization improvement must correlate with token/sec increase; otherwise investigate memory stalls.

PROFILING PLAYBOOK (when criteria fail)
1) If P99 jumps: enable full trace (1ms sampling) for a 2-minute window around tail events.
2) Correlate tail with kernel maps: check for long matmul spikes or attention kernel stalls.
3) Inspect scheduler queue: is time spent in queue vs. running? If queue wait dominates, examine batch slice policy.
4) If memory fragmentation suspected: run memscan and simulate evictions with a staging job.

SAFETY / ROLLBACK CHECKLIST
- Keep the dedicated test pool isolated; do not promote to prod until reviewed.
- If runtime-level changes are applied to production inadvertently: set routing policy to fallback model variant and pauase autoscaler: "routectl set-fallback --model stable-1 --reason=emergency".
- On GPU OOM or watchdog: kill offending pods and re-deploy prior image. Document incident with run-id and artifacts.

REPORTING AND ARTIFACTS
Required artifacts saved to s3://redwood-benchshots/{run-id}/:
- baseline.json, run-config.yaml, perf-trace.tar.gz, kernel-timelines/*.trace, bench-report.pdf, bench-metrics.csv.
Include a 1-page executive summary with clear recommendation: accept/no-accept/needs-more-work and the primary root cause.

COMMUNICATIONS & REVIEW
- Post quick summary in #eng-runtime-bench with run-id and top-line metrics within 24 hours.
- Send full report to reviewers and schedule a 30-minute triage within 48 hours.

APPENDIX: Helpful commands
- Start collector: perfctl start --target=pool-a --sampling-ms=100 --out /tmp/{run-id}
- Kernel dump: kern-dump --run {run-id} --filter attention,matmul --out /tmp/{run-id}/kdump
- Produce report: bench-report --input /tmp/{run-id} --out /tmp/{run-id}/report.pdf

RELATED PAGES AND REFERENCES
- See also: Mixed workload SLO simulation (simulation suite) for synthetic generator parameters.
- Runtime telemetry data model: defines event ids and kernel annotations used by bench-report.

REVISION HISTORY
- 2025-11-12: created by Aisha Kapoor (initial protocol).
- 2026-02-10: updated acceptance criteria and added KV cache degraded mode (Marcus Li).

END OF DOCUMENT
